quizzes.title: Electron Configuration
quizzes.description: 30 questions on complete ground-state electron configurations of neutral atoms, without noble-gas abbreviations.

questions.prompt: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of a neutral hydrogen atom (H)?
questions.explanation: A neutral hydrogen atom has 1 electron. Its ground-state electron configuration is 1s¹.

questions.prompt: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of a neutral helium atom (He)?
questions.explanation: A neutral helium atom has 2 electrons. Its ground-state electron configuration is 1s².

questions.prompt: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of a neutral lithium atom (Li)?

questions.prompt: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of a neutral beryllium atom (Be)?
questions.explanation: A neutral beryllium atom has 4 electrons. Its ground-state electron configuration is 1s² 2s².

questions.explanation: A neutral boron atom has 5 electrons. Its ground-state electron configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p¹.

questions.explanation: A neutral carbon atom has 6 electrons. Its ground-state electron configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p².

questions.prompt: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of a neutral calcium atom (Ca)?

He.name: Helium
He.fact: Lowest boiling point of all elements.

Si.name: Silicon
Si.fact: Second most abundant element in Earth's crust.

Br.name: Bromine
Br.fact: Only nonmetal liquid at room temperature.

Mo.name: Molybdenum
Mo.fact: Has a very high melting point.

Ag.name: Silver
Ag.fact: Highest electrical conductivity of any element.

Cd.name: Cadmium
Cd.uses: Batteries and cadmium telluride solar cells.

Xe.name: Xenon
Xe.fact: Can form compounds despite being a noble gas.

La.name: Lanthanum
La.fact: Its name means to lie hidden.

Ce.name: Cerium
Ce.fact: Most abundant rare-earth element in Earth's crust.

Nd.name: Neodymium
Nd.uses: Magnets in headphones and electric motors.
